body:
## Problem Statement

The Operator needs to inspect, control and restart Dalph while an unfinished Run has a large Journal, active executor work and slow observers. Expensive historical preparation or stalled output can obscure current state and delay local control handling. When work cannot settle, the Operator needs the exact missing evidence rather than a generic waiting or timeout message.

The business outcome is affordable observation, responsive controls, actionable ownership diagnostics and reliable restart within the current supported data format. These preserve already completed work and prevent duplicate external actions. The project currently has no external users: cross-release data migration and compatibility with old Journal formats are not required for this scope. The Operator may explicitly discard obsolete development data; that is never evidence that external work stopped.

## Solution

The Operator reads a coherent current status independently of optional historical expansion, reconnects to the latest accepted observation, and requests bounded historical pages when details are needed. Slow clients have bounded retention and cannot delay control admission. Pause, Cancel and Exit retain their different meanings; receipt, application and safe settlement are visibly distinct.

When a control or restart cannot complete, Dalph identifies the exact responsibility and missing boundary evidence. Restart with retained current-format data reconstructs the same Run and reconciles uncertain operations before another effect. Incompatible development data is refused before effects, with an explicit explanation that the Operator can retire or discard it separately after resolving external custody.

Existing improvements remain part of the acceptance baseline. Implement only the missing behavior and qualify the combined Operator outcome; do not rebuild already working publication, control or recovery protocols.

## User Stories

1. As an Operator, I want current Run status without expanding the entire history, so that I can see progress promptly.
2. As an Operator, I want status to remain coherent at a known accepted observation, so that I do not act on a mixture of unrelated revisions.
3. As an Operator, I want historical details on demand, so that routine monitoring stays affordable.
4. As an Operator, I want bounded historical pages with exact continuation information, so that a long Run remains inspectable.
5. As an Operator, I want oversized historical responses to be identified explicitly, so that I know whether I received a complete answer.
6. As an Operator, I want malformed history to fail explicitly even when an answer would exceed its quota, so that size limits cannot conceal corruption.
7. As an Operator, I want a slow client to retain bounded pending data, so that it does not exhaust the host.
8. As an Operator, I want reconnect to provide current committed state, so that I can recover observation without replaying workflow actions.
9. As an Operator, I want skipped intermediate watch updates to remain distinguishable from lossless history, so that I do not mistake a live view for an audit log.
10. As an Operator, I want an observer disconnect to leave task execution unchanged, so that closing a browser does not cancel work.
11. As an Operator, I want explicit admission limits for observers, so that excess clients receive a useful refusal rather than degrading all clients.
12. As an Operator, I want Pause accepted while historical computation is busy, so that I can stop further progress admission.
13. As an Operator, I want Pause application distinguished from safe-boundary confirmation, so that I know which work is still settling.
14. As an Operator, I want Cancel to preserve its exact stop and claim-settlement requirements, so that cancellation cannot lose resources or duplicate work.
15. As a Supervisor, I want Exit to work during startup before Run selection, so that resource acquisition remains controllable.
16. As a Supervisor, I want repeated Exit to join the original deadline, so that repeated signals cannot prolong shutdown.
17. As an Operator, I want stalled output to have a bounded shutdown allowance, so that an unread pipe cannot keep the application alive indefinitely.
18. As an Operator, I want typed timeout and transport failures preserved, so that an unsuccessful boundary is not shown as successful shutdown.
19. As an Operator, I want local handling time separated from provider waiting time, so that I can identify the cause of slow progress.
20. As an Operator, I want blocked progress to name the exact task, attempt, operation or resource, so that I can investigate the correct subject.
21. As an Operator, I want the missing observation or stopped-writer proof explained, so that I know what must happen before continuation.
22. As an Operator, I want the permitted next action explained, so that I do not accidentally repeat an uncertain mutation.
23. As an Operator, I want executing, safely suspended, terminal, unavailable and contradictory evidence distinguished, so that absence is not mistaken for safety.
24. As an Operator, I want independent work to continue when a blocker is local, so that one disputed resource does not halt unrelated tasks.
25. As an Operator, I want diagnostics to omit credentials and private provider content, so that I can share them for troubleshooting.
26. As an Operator, I want restart with retained current-format data to reconstruct the same Run and attempts, so that a crash does not erase progress.
27. As an Operator, I want an uncertain tracker, Git or executor effect reconciled at its original authority, so that restart does not repeat unsafe work.
28. As an Operator, I want exclusive ownership across stop and restart, so that old and new storage writers cannot overlap.
29. As an Operator, I want incompatible development data refused before effects, so that a new binary cannot silently reinterpret old obligations.
30. As an Operator, I want freedom to explicitly discard obsolete development data instead of migrating it, so that pre-release changes do not require a compatibility programme.
31. As an Operator, I want a reset to leave external custody and resources governed by their existing protocols, so that removing local data is not permission to start duplicate work or clean dirty worktrees.
32. As a Maintainer, I want declared workload and resource measurements tied to the candidate, so that improvements can be assessed without treating a small unit test as system acceptance.

## Implementation Decisions

### Scope and authorities

- Keep tracker task lifecycle, dependencies and claims in the tracker; Git lineage, refs, worktrees and publication evidence in Git; session/process observations in the execution substrate; workflow history in the Journal.
- Preserve the protected separation between delivery description, action planning and runtime admission. Passive observation gains no scheduling, mutation, retry or cleanup capability.
- Preserve distinct responsibility subjects. A blocker or timeout for one subject cannot settle another subject on the same attempt.
- Use idiomatic Effect V4, typed errors and branded boundary identities, positions, locators, capacities and durations. Diagnostics and caches are derived process-local values.
- The new spec supersedes the earlier blanket requirement to preserve unfinished Runs through incompatible release formats for this pre-release scope. It does not revoke existing current-format recovery or accepted safe cleanup requirements.
- Journal event versions such as 14 and 15 are internal stored-event contracts, not product release numbers. No package-version bump is required by this feature. Format changes are allowed without old-data migration; an incompatible format must still be detected rather than silently interpreted.
- Existing historical decoding may remain where already implemented; this issue neither expands its support nor orders its removal. No actual data deletion is part of implementation or publication of this specification.
- Archive retention and compact completion-record policy are owned by the existing archive issues. This work preserves them and does not promise indefinite availability of retired historical pages.

### Affordable observation

- Use the existing coherent current-status and accepted-history boundaries. Historical pages are read-only and fixed to an exact Run and accepted cursor; continuation stays on that same prefix rather than blending later records into earlier pages.
- Coalesce pending passive historical notifications to the latest cursor. Do not enqueue full historical snapshots. Preserve existing per-host subscriber admission and explicit overload errors.
- Bound retained bytes as well as item counts. Include the value under preparation, the admitted transport write and a single oversized input in accounting; queue length alone is insufficient.
- Retain existing CLI limits of 1 MiB per historical snapshot and 8 MiB per invocation. Reject expensive optional expansion from validated affordability evidence and preserve the exact cursor-only fallback. Do not globally apply CLI output quotas to required status facts or unrelated transports.
- Add bounded on-demand historical paging at the existing public history boundary. A page identifies its fixed prefix, covered range, completion and continuation; it never claims to be the full trace when partial. Unsupported query or capacity has a typed refusal. An indivisible value that exceeds a page budget is reported explicitly rather than returned in an unbounded page.
- Preserve whole-record publication ordering. Reconnect starts a new current-first observation; a convergent watch is not advertised as a lossless event stream. Explicit historical reads provide retained audit facts separately.
- Reuse successful immutable prefix preparation and bounded ephemeral indexes. Restart discards them and validates persisted current-format history. Durable reconstruction checkpoints are not selected.

### Responsive controls

- Expensive optional history preparation stays outside output serialization and yields between bounded checked chunks. Never weaken canonical validation to meet a timing target.
- Separate command receipt, durable application and safe settlement. Use existing Applied control direction and Pause progress vocabulary; do not label a received request as an applied command.
- Pause, cancellation and application Exit retain existing admission and settlement protocols. Observer cancellation affects only observation.
- Retain the five-second application Exit drain from the original cutoff. Retain the selected maximum 500 ms output allowance after lifecycle-result availability, capped by the remaining original deadline; TimedOut receives no extra allowance. A stalled receiver can lose partial/final output, which is not a successful flush.
- Keep early-startup Exit connected to the same application shell without inventing a Run identity. Finalization failures preserve failure status even if the lifecycle result was Succeeded.
- Use the existing provisional engineering target of p95 local admission opportunity at or below 100 ms and initial 10 ms cooperative work quantum on a declared reference profile. These are measured targets, not external stop proofs, new hard timeouts or universal real-time guarantees. Report failure to meet them explicitly.

### Actionable ownership

- Reuse current delivery status, Pause progress and lifecycle ownership observations. Extend their derived diagnostics with exact scope and correlation, boundary family, last accepted relevant evidence, missing proof or contradiction, and the next action permitted by the owning protocol.
- Make local processing, external execution/waiting, uncertain outcome, safe settlement and refused continuation distinguishable. Do not invent a progress percentage or ETA from process age.
- A blocked control or timeout exposes relevant unresolved subjects; a local contradiction only blocks regions whose next action requires the disputed evidence. Shared ownership or invalid history may block the whole Run.
- Protect credentials, prompts and provider-private payloads. Expose only identifiers and evidence summaries needed for diagnosis. Reading diagnostics causes no authority calls or effects.

### Current-format recovery and development resets

- Reconstruct the same Run, attempt, immutable Base, worktree and operation identities from complete retained current-format history before new workflow admission.
- Reconcile each uncertain external outcome at its owning boundary before any retry. Unavailable, foreign or contradictory evidence retains responsibility and produces its exact diagnostic.
- Never overlap old and new coordinator, Journal or executor storage owners. Process exit or disappearance alone is not a general stopped-descendant or safe-suspension proof.
- Incompatible stored formats fail before workflow effects and explain the supported format and separate development reset option. Never automatically wipe data, fabricate a new beginning over rejected history or silently upgrade records.
- Explicit manual retirement of obsolete data is allowed for this stage; it does not authorize deletion of external claims, worktrees or provider resources. No new reset command is required. If external ownership remains uncertain, preserve the custody evidence and resolve it through the existing owner before starting competing work.

### Operational scenarios and acceptance mapping

These scenarios preserve existing governing protocols and specify the additional combined outcomes. Scope acceptance includes their forbidden results; the Operator confirmed the public production-host seam with physical CLI/SQLite controls on 2026-10-09.

| Scenario | Starting facts and trigger | Ordered boundary calls and visible result | Crash or retry and forbidden result | Acceptance test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 Read status during expensive history | One unfinished Run has retained executor work and a valid large/dense Journal; Alice requests history and current status | Read the committed prefix for history; obtain coherent current status independently; check affordability before optional full expansion; show complete status and either bounded history or exact cursor fallback | Observer restart repeats reads only; malformed history fails rather than hiding behind a size refusal; no tracker/Git/executor mutation | Public host acceptance: current status remains available during controlled blocked/large historical preparation; exact full/fallback parity and malformed-prefix rejection |
| A2 Slow client and reconnect | Alice watches Run R; R advances while the receiver stalls, disconnects and reconnects | Deliver a current-first frame; retain bounded pending cursors/bytes; release the disconnected subscription; reconnect from coherent latest state; read older details separately | Reconnect after host restart uses reconstructed committed observations; no unbounded backlog, invented contiguous audit stream, partial state labelled complete or execution cancellation | Public watch acceptance: blocked writer, subscription refusal/release, disconnect and reconnect with latest state; native slow-consumer resource profile |
| A3 Browse retained history in pages | A retained current-format prefix contains more history than one permitted response; Alice requests a page and continuation while new records arrive | Fix the original cursor, validate it, check page capacity, return range/completion/continuation; continuation reads the same prefix; report individually oversized values or unavailable retained history explicitly | Retrying a read has no effects; a corrupt/gapped prefix fails; later appends cannot create duplicates/gaps inside that fixed prefix | Public history acceptance: concatenate bounded pages and compare canonical original-prefix content; append-between-pages, oversized value and invalid continuation controls |
| C1 Pause or Cancel during observation | Run R has executing work, exact claim and busy optional historical preparation; Alice requests Pause or Cancel | Admit through existing control boundary; record/apply the existing direction; publish receipt/application separately from progress; perform exact suspension, claim and cancellation settlement calls only as required by that command | Crash around external calls retains exact intent and reconciles before repetition; no timeout-based release, observer-induced delivery cancellation or new forward work barred by the control | Production host control acceptance: busy reader plus Pause safe-boundary progress; Cancel exact suspension/claim settlement; unavailable executor evidence negative control |
| C2 Exit with stalled output or during acquisition | The host may own coordinator/Journal resources before Run selection, or has an admitted output write and active local owners; Supervisor sends SIGTERM twice | Same shell receives the first cutoff; seal admission; drain exact owners; cancel optional preparation; allow admitted output within the original deadline; finalize resources; report exact lifecycle/process outcome when transport permits | Repeated signal joins the original cutoff; interruption retains unresolved custody; no invented Run, fresh deadline, success over finalizer failure, claimed flush or inferred safe executor stop | Built CLI/native acceptance: pre-selection Exit, draining/released/stalled/closed stdout, unresolved drain, repeated signals, failing finalizer, exact child/group and lock evidence |
| O1 Explain an unresolved responsibility | A control or recovery cannot settle one exact attempt because required executor/Git/tracker evidence is absent or contradictory; Alice reads status/progress | Read coherent derived diagnostics; name exact subject and missing proof; expose permitted next step and separate unrelated work; update after conclusive accepted evidence | Reconnect rederives diagnostics; no diagnostic persistence as authority, retry permission from elapsed time, foreign subject release or secret disclosure | Public status/progress acceptance: unavailable/foreign/contradictory evidence, independent task continues, redaction, diagnostic disappears only after applicable settlement |
| R1 Restart after an ambiguous effect | Current-format history has exact tracker/Git/executor intent; its authority applied the effect but acknowledgement was not durably observed; Supervisor stops and restarts Dalph | Prove exclusive ownership, read/decode/reduce complete history, retain the same subject, reconcile at the original authority, then record observation or remain blocked | A second cut repeats required authoritative reads with the same identity; no duplicate Begin, unsafe mutation, new attempt, omitted corruption or stale authority substitution | Public production recovery acceptance: authority-specific crash cuts, same identity/effect count, exact obligations and unavailable-evidence negative controls; native SQLite reopen and process custody |
| R2 Encounter obsolete development data | Alice starts the current binary with an incompatible Journal, then elects to retire that development dataset separately | Acquire appropriate ownership, inspect/decode, refuse incompatible history before workflow effects and explain the supported format/reset option; only a separately authorised and safely isolated empty dataset starts a fresh Run | Lost startup response never permits automatic deletion; reset interrupted or external writers uncertain means no competing ownership; no migration, silent reinterpretation or claim/worktree cleanup inferred from data absence | Production startup acceptance: unsupported-format refusal and zero workflow effects; fresh isolated dataset works; disputed old-owner control remains blocked; assert no files are deleted by refusal |

The same-format scenarios are applicable without package releases or migrations. Observer disconnect does not add a durable workflow event. For historical paging, crash recovery concerns only reading retained committed facts; no external mutation retry is applicable. R2 specifies detection and existing manual retirement boundaries, not a destructive automatic reset workflow.

## Testing Decisions

- Prefer one shared acceptance seam: the existing public production repository host, reached through its CLI/HTTP clients with controlled tracker, Git and executor adapters. Test what the Operator receives and which owning-boundary effects occur; do not assert internal fiber count, cache shape or incidental call order.
- Use controlled gates and TestClock for causal control/output races and exact deadlines. Use the highest existing seam for all A/C/O/R scenarios. Targeted pure/schema tests supplement it only for invalid inputs, paging equivalence and redaction that would be expensive to enumerate through processes.
- Use the existing real Node/CLI subprocess fixtures as physical evidence beneath that same seam for signal receipt, stalled pipes, storage reopen, lock release and exact writer/descendant absence. Mocked cancellation cannot prove these facts. Real browser coverage is needed only for changed browser rendering or interaction.
- Prior art includes current-first running-host watches with slow-writer/reconnect and subscription-limit controls, production inspection/Exit acceptance, CLI output-grace/native signal controls, Pause progress, production public recovery and canonical Journal corruption/reopening tests.
- Each scenario row names its required acceptance test. Implementation handoff must map the row to exact passing test names and candidate evidence, including deliberately unexecuted suffixes. Aggregate test totals do not replace this mapping.
- Declare workload profiles by records, stored/decoded bytes, causal edges, tracker size, unfinished obligations and observer count. Use controlled bulk fixtures and minimal live-provider acceptance; never retry throttled mutations.
- Measure cold restart separately from warm status/control/history: CPU and wall time, p95 local admission, peak RSS/heap, retained cache/pending bytes, output size and preparation counts. Record candidate, Node, reference machine, fixture and stopped-writer evidence. A queue of one or a small fixture is not proof of a byte or production capacity bound.
- Use the selected isolated measurement safety envelope of 1 GiB Node heap and 1.5 GiB RSS, excluding executor children; report exceeded or unproven targets rather than dropping facts. Establish candidate-specific budgets before claiming measured capacity. Do not treat one timing sample as p95.
- Choose focused owner and affected-consumer checks for each coherent slice. Protocol/formal changes require existing applicable model and conformance controls. Whole-system acceptance covers all scenario rows and declared resource profiles; an expensive broad gate requires its separate agreed qualification scope.

## Out of Scope

- Integrating Pi Durable, replacing Codex App Server or replacing Dalph's workflow algebra.
- Cross-release compatibility guarantees, new legacy migration/backfill, multi-version rollback matrices and a product release-version bump.
- A new destructive reset command or deletion of any existing development data during this work.
- Durable frontier/status caches, persistent UI state or reconstruction checkpoints that bypass complete current-format validation.
- Automatic force pushes, reintegration, unsafe mutation retries or disposal authorised by a timeout.
- New archive retention policies, completion-summary storage or work already owned by archive issues #487–#490.
- A universal hard real-time SLA, provider execution deadline or isolation architecture without discriminating measurements and separately accepted scenarios.
- Redesigning authentication, remote access or unrelated browser UX.

## Further Notes

Owner decisions from this conversation: all four business outcomes are selected; synthesize without another interview; pre-release data may be explicitly discarded and legacy compatibility is optional. Current-format crash recovery and exact external custody remain mandatory.

The Operator confirmed the public production-host seam with physical CLI/SQLite controls on 2026-10-09. Tracker owns task status and dependency planning. Existing issues #486 and #487–#490 retain their own scope; this specification covers their combined-outcome boundaries only where stated.

Implementation must reconcile planning documents that still require blanket legacy preservation with this narrower accepted pre-release policy, while preserving accepted current-format scenarios and any already implemented legacy reader. Documentation alignment changes no runtime behavior on its own.


## Parent delivery and completion

Execute native child issues #492–#500 independently, then #501 after all nine complete. This parent is natively blocked by #501; subissue grouping alone grants no completion order.

After #501 is delivered, this parent owns final combined acceptance: verify all eight governing scenarios and declared measurements against the exact integrated candidate, preserve scoped reviews and explicit limits, reconcile accepted pre-release documentation, and retain the final scenario-to-test/evidence ledger. Do not reimplement child slices or repeat unchanged broad checks without a named affected boundary. A failed p95/capacity claim remains unaccepted until scoped repair or an explicit owner decision; aggregate totals and merely reporting a miss are insufficient.
title: Keep observation affordable and controls responsive with exact ownership diagnostics and current-format recovery

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

The Operator requests historical occurrences through an additive read-only host/client operation, with fixed-prefix continuation and explicit size or availability refusal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A1/A3: page ordered existing historical occurrences at exact RunId and committedThrough; declare covered positions, complete/partial status and continuation. Concatenated pages equal the canonical occurrence sequence at that prefix, including a new append between requests.
- [ ] Use initial maximum 1 MiB UTF-8 for the whole encoded response, including envelope; allow smaller supported requests. Do not build a complete historical graph/facets/relationships view just to slice it. Graph/facet pagination is outside this slice.
- [ ] An indivisible oversized occurrence yields typed refusal with exact identity and available size information; do not skip it or advance continuation past it. Bad/foreign cursor, malformed prefix and unsupported capacity fail explicitly.
- [ ] Current coherent status remains available during optional page preparation. Invalid history cannot be masked by quota fallback; existing full-view/cursor-only behavior is preserved.
- [ ] Public production-host/client tests prove all above, zero tracker/Git/executor mutation on reads, and archive-owner historical-unavailability behavior. Preserve CLI cumulative output quota separately from logical history across multiple invocations.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Read bounded historical occurrence pages from one committed Run prefix

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

A stalled client consumes bounded observer-owned resources, receives explicit overload/refusal and reconnects to current coherent state without affecting task execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A2: declare and enforce observer-owned budgets for pending work, disposable preparation and encoded/admitted writes; account separately for shared canonical state. Retaining one pending value alone is not the byte bound.
- [ ] Preserve current-first delivery, existing subscription admission, whole-record ordering, disconnect slot release and latest-state reconnect. Do not advertise coalesced watch updates as a contiguous audit stream.
- [ ] A required current-state value beyond transport capacity produces typed refusal, never silent truncation or a historical cursor-only substitute. Preserve existing transport limits unless a separately accepted change is necessary.
- [ ] Native slow-reader profiles demonstrate retained-byte behavior and exact release; public watch tests prove refusal, reconnect and no workflow mutation or observer-induced work cancellation.
- [ ] Declare profile/candidate and report total RSS separately from enforceable optional-retention bounds; do not claim a universal heap cap from the experiment safety ceiling. No dependency on historical paging unless actual shared functionality is proven necessary.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Keep slow current-state observers within declared optional retention limits

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

The Operator sees which exact subject is blocked, what evidence is missing and what the owning protocol permits next.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] O1: reuse current delivery status and Pause progress vocabulary. Public diagnostics name scope/correlation, boundary family, last relevant accepted evidence, missing proof or contradiction and next permitted step.
- [ ] Controlled unavailable, foreign and contradictory executor/tracker/Git evidence remains distinguishable from executing, safe or terminal evidence; no timeout, generic absence or unrelated subject settles responsibility.
- [ ] One task-local blocker leaves an independent task able to continue; diagnostics update only when relevant accepted evidence changes. Existing sufficiently descriptive variants are reused instead of duplicated.
- [ ] Public status tests prove exact correlation, redaction of secrets/provider-private content, and zero authority calls or mutations caused by reading diagnostics. No persisted derived diagnostic state, ETA or generic retry authorization.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Explain exact unresolved responsibilities in current public status

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

The Operator or Supervisor gets exact redacted owner diagnostics while the application lives and in Exit output when delivery succeeds, with unchanged shutdown and custody semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] C2/O1: identify admitted owners and missing drain evidence, including provider/Journal/local-action ownership and pre-selection NoRun. Derive diagnostics from existing lifecycle owners; add no durable Exit-report mailbox.
- [ ] Preserve original five-second cutoff, repeated-signal behavior, bounded 500 ms output allowance, no extra allowance for TimedOut, and failure status for finalizer or transport failure.
- [ ] Stalled output may omit diagnostics and final records; do not promise retrieval from a dead host. Restart rederives durable unsettled responsibilities through ordinary recovery.
- [ ] Reuse accepted #486 grace and early-startup Exit implementation and evidence rather than rebuilding it because the tracker issue remains open. Native relevant controls prove exact process/descendant and lock evidence; a non-cooperative owner retains custody.
- [ ] Public/native tests prove named owner correlation, redaction, draining/stalled/closed output, repeated Exit, unresolved drain and finalization failure. No inferred Run finality or safe suspension from process termination.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Explain unresolved Exit owners without extending shutdown or promising output delivery

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

The Operator sends attached whole-Run Pause or Cancel to the running owner and distinguishes accepted/applied controls from safe settlement, even during expensive history work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] C1: explicitly add attached whole-Run Pause and Cancel through the existing host command mechanism and public clients. Existing offline Cancel is not invoked as a competing coordinator against the active owner. Reuse accepted control/cancellation protocols, not a second implementation.
- [ ] Define exact request/Run/host correlation and ambiguous-response behavior before effects. Receipt is not Applied control direction; application is not safe-boundary confirmation or completed cancellation.
- [ ] Busy optional historical work cannot bar local admission. Pause seals its existing covered forward admission; Cancel retains exact executor stop, abandonment disposition, claim settlement and Run termination requirements.
- [ ] Unavailable/foreign executor reports keep responsibility and expose existing progress/status rather than false completion. Disconnecting the command client does not authorize unsafe retransmission or erase admitted control.
- [ ] Public production-host/client acceptance exercises busy history, receipt/application/settlement, ambiguous reply and unavailable evidence; native repeated declared profiles measure local admission separately from provider latency against provisional targets. Existing offline Cancel remains valid.
- [ ] Map full chronology and scoped tests before runtime changes; do not add task-scoped controls or new authorization policy. Reuse existing progress fields without waiting on slice 03 unless its new fields are genuinely required.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Apply whole-Run Pause and Cancel to the owning host while observation is busy

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

After the tracker applies an exact claim but Dalph loses the acknowledgement and stops, restart recognizes that same claim without issuing another mutation or starting a duplicate attempt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] R1 tracker cut: persist exact acquisition intent; tracker applies claim; stop before conclusive outcome persistence; reopen current-format Journal under exclusive ownership and reconcile the same subject at the tracker.
- [ ] Retain same Run, plan where already recorded, operation and claim identity; accepted exact matching evidence permits continuation without a second mutation. Unreadable, foreign or contradictory evidence remains blocked with applicable public explanation.
- [ ] A second cut during reconciliation repeats required reads, not unsafe acquisition. Preserve dependency eligibility and current tracker authority.
- [ ] Reuse mapped claim recovery-prefix/cassette tests. Add only missing composed public-host and physical-storage evidence; identify what each retained test already proves before repair. No new general tracker recovery engine or all-operation subprocess matrix.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Prove same-Run restart after an ambiguously applied tracker claim acquisition

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

Restart recognizes the same candidate already published to the pinned branch and continues the original delivery without a duplicate push or changed candidate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] R1 Git cut: persist exact publication intent; receiving branch accepts the exact candidate; lose the send response before conclusive Journal observation; stop/reopen with proven sender custody.
- [ ] Reconcile pinned same-endpoint branch ancestry for the original candidate and operation before another push; retain Run, candidate, pin and original Git facts. Publication proof, local promotion and tracker completion retain their accepted ordering.
- [ ] Unavailable/contradictory Git evidence retains the exact wait and permits no force push, automatic mutation retry or fabricated publication. A further cut preserves the same identity.
- [ ] Reuse direct-publication and retained-prefix conformance evidence. Fill only the missing public restart/custody proof with controlled authority and minimal native Git fixture; do not duplicate broad Git recovery or use live bulk provider calls.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Prove same-Run restart after a remote publication loses its acknowledgement

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

After the executor accepted Begin but its acknowledgement is lost, restart reattaches to the same work instead of launching another turn or releasing its position.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] R1 executor cut: record Begin for exact planned attempt; substrate accepts work; cut before conclusive outcome persistence; reopen the current-format Journal and reconcile exact command/session before admission.
- [ ] Preserve Run, Attempt, Base, branch/worktree and command identity. Executing work is observed without a second semantic Begin or Resume; safe/terminal reports follow their existing protocols.
- [ ] Unavailable, foreign, unreadable or inconclusive absence retains responsibility. Preserve the separately accepted conclusive empty pre-turn association recovery rule rather than banning its proven same-Begin redelivery.
- [ ] Native owner/descendant/storage evidence excludes overlapping writers; coordinator loss and whole-substrate loss remain distinct cases. No PID/timeout-only proof of safe suspension.
- [ ] Audit existing production public recovery and executor reconciliation tests first; fill the exact lost-acknowledgement composition gap and report candidate-specific public/native evidence without rebuilding the executor.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Prove current-format restart of an ambiguous executor Begin with exclusive custody

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/dalph/issues/491

## What to build

The Operator sees a clear unsupported-format refusal and can use a separately retired isolated dataset without a migration requirement or automatic deletion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] R2: startup detects incompatible stored semantics and reports supported format before tracker/Git/executor workflow effects; retain source bytes and do not create a new Run beginning over rejected history.
- [ ] A safely isolated fresh current-format dataset starts normally; disputed previous ownership remains blocked. Missing local data is not evidence that external claims, dirty worktrees, sessions or writers disappeared.
- [ ] No reset command, automatic data wipe, legacy migration or product package-version bump. Existing historical decoding may remain without expansion or forced removal.
- [ ] Align planning documentation that still requires blanket legacy preservation with the accepted no-migration pre-release scope. Preserve existing current-format recovery, accepted cleanup rules and separate archive scopes.
- [ ] Public startup/native ownership tests prove useful refusal, zero forbidden workflow effects, no file deletion and isolated fresh startup; focused documentation checks validate updated guidance.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Refuse incompatible development history before effects and align the reset policy

body:
## Supported-use failure threatening #491

An actual #491 production Run safely suspended #495 after an interrupted Codex turn. A tool item from that original turn retained Started when its completion notification was lost at interruption. The owning coordinator later resumed the same planned attempt. Its new turn was interrupted after 2.5 seconds when the old item's expired timer stopped the shared containment. A retained LimitReached for the original turn now makes passive observation Unreadable while the Journal's last report remains Executing. StartWork does not resolve that exact ownership responsibility. No history or native custody records have been edited.

Evidence is retained locally under `/workspace/dalph-dogfood/issue-491-20261009/evidence/issue-495-tool-custody-diagnostic.json`, continuation snapshots, stderr completion metadata, and the native per-attempt store. Original turn `01a122b3-c44e-7671-ae97-676ccd833049`; resumed turn `01a122d2-2cc5-7163-9757-3ab45465148b`. Both belong to thread `01a122b3-c180-7802-91c9-077badfde455` and one immutable Run/Attempt/Task/Worktree. Original limit was recorded as Elapsed; stop completion was retained. Do not infer future stopped custody from this timestamp alone.

## Required outcome and boundaries
